faqs.question: What does HLA cross-match by Flow cytometry measure?
faqs.answer: HLA cross-match by flow cytometry measures the surface markers present on your immune cells called human leucocyte antigens (HLA) that help identify self-cells from foreign cells.

faqs.question: Why is HLA cross-match by Flow cytometry done?
faqs.answer: • To assess the compatibility of a donor's and recipient's immune system before an organ transplantation • To monitor the effectiveness of immunosuppressive therapy after a transplant • To detect and diagnose autoimmune disorders like diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, celiac disease, etc. • To investigate transfusion reactions, when blood products can trigger an adverse immune response

faqs.question: When is HLA cross-match recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if you • are scheduled for an organ transplant, • have symptoms or a family history of autoimmune disorders, or • experience transfusion reactions or complications after blood transfusions.

faqs.question: What if the results of the HLA cross-match are abnormal?
faqs.answer: The results of the HLA cross-match can be either compatible or incompatible between the donor and recipient. If it's incompatible, it may result in the rejection of an organ transplant or immune-mediated complications.

faqs.question: What to expect during the HLA cross-match?
faqs.answer: • Blood samples will be collected from both the recipient and donor. • The samples will be processed in the laboratory through flow cytometry.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the HLA cross-match?
faqs.answer: • Avoid medications that can interfere with your test results. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with HLA cross-match?
faqs.answer: • Complete Blood Count (CBC) • Serum creatinine levels • Liver function tests • Additional HLA testing, such as HLA typing

faqs.question: What is the HLA cross-match by Flow cytometry also known as?
faqs.answer: Histocompatibility testing or HLA compatibility testing

faqs.question: What is organ transplantation?
faqs.answer: Organ transplantation is a surgical procedure where an organ from one person (donor) is transplanted into another person's (recipient) body to replace a damaged or diseased organ. Common examples include liver, kidney, heart, lungs or pancreas transplants.
